Answer: B
Reason: Comparing the pre-operative chest X-ray (Figure 1a), which shows a relatively normal mediastinum, with the post-operative image (Figure 3a) reveals a significant new or enlarged widening of the superior mediastinum. In the context of a known thyroid angiosarcoma, this rapid increase in mediastinal size shortly after surgery is most indicative of an aggressive tumor recurrence rather than a benign post-surgical change like a hematoma or successful removal.
